quests.instruction: Which one do you carry on your back to bring your things to school?
quests.hint: Look for the one with two straps that go over your shoulders.
quests.explanation: A backpack holds your books and supplies, and the straps keep your hands free for walking.
quests.funFact: Wearing a backpack on both shoulders spreads its weight more evenly than carrying it on one.

quests.instruction: Who stands at the front of the room and teaches the lesson?
quests.hint: This person plans lessons and helps the class understand new ideas.
quests.explanation: Teachers plan lessons, explain new ideas, and help students when they get stuck.
quests.funFact: The word 'teach' comes from an Old English word meaning 'to show'.

quests.instruction: Which room is where your class has most of its lessons?
quests.hint: It has desks, a board, and your teacher.
quests.explanation: The classroom is your main learning space, where your class sits together and works.
quests.funFact: Class sizes differ around the world, from just a few students to more than thirty.

quests.instruction: Which writing tool has a sharp point and makes soft gray marks?
quests.hint: Check the tip. Inside the wood is a soft gray core.
quests.explanation: A pencil leaves gray graphite marks, and the point needs sharpening when it gets dull.
quests.funFact: The 'lead' in a pencil is graphite mixed with clay. There is no metal lead inside.

quests.instruction: Which one is made of colored wax and is great for coloring big pictures?
quests.hint: It feels smooth and waxy, and it comes in many colors.
quests.explanation: Crayons are made of colored wax, so they glide across paper and fill large spaces quickly.
quests.funFact: Crayons are mostly wax, which is why they soften if they are left somewhere hot.

quests.instruction: You made a mistake in your pencil drawing. What can fix it?
quests.hint: It rubs the mark away without tearing the paper.
quests.explanation: An eraser rubs pencil marks off the page. Marker ink is too strong to be erased this way.
quests.funFact: Before rubber erasers, people rubbed pencil marks away with pieces of bread.

quests.instruction: Which one has blank pages joined together so you can write your own work?
quests.hint: Look for pages that are empty and ready to be filled.
quests.explanation: A notebook's blank lined pages are for your own writing, like spelling words or notes.
quests.funFact: The lines in a notebook help keep your handwriting neat and the same size.

quests.instruction: Which one is filled with stories and pictures made by an author?
quests.hint: Someone wrote and printed it so that other people could read it.
quests.explanation: Books are written by authors and drawn by illustrators, so we read them to enjoy or to learn.
quests.funFact: Many picture books have exactly 32 pages.

quests.instruction: Which one keeps loose worksheets together so they don't get lost?
quests.hint: It has flat covers that hold papers that are not stapled or sewn.
quests.explanation: A folder keeps loose papers flat and together, so worksheets don't get crumpled in your bag.
quests.funFact: Folders are often color-coded so people can find the right one quickly.

quests.instruction: Which tool has two blades and cuts paper?
quests.hint: The two blades slide past each other when you squeeze the handles.
quests.explanation: Scissors cut when their two blades close together. Carry them with the blades pointing down.
quests.funFact: People have used scissors for thousands of years.

quests.instruction: Which one makes paper stick to paper when you rub it on?
quests.hint: You twist the bottom to push up the sticky stick.
quests.explanation: A glue stick adds a thin sticky layer. Press the papers together for a moment so they hold.
quests.funFact: The first glue stick went on sale in 1969.

quests.instruction: Which tool joins several pages with a small piece of metal?
quests.hint: You press down on it and a small metal piece goes through the pages.
quests.explanation: A stapler pushes a staple through the pages and folds its ends flat so the pages stay together.
quests.funFact: A stapler bends the ends of each staple so they lie flat against the paper.

quests.instruction: Where do you run, climb, and swing during outdoor play?
quests.hint: It is outside, and it has equipment like slides and swings.
quests.explanation: The playground is where students get fresh air and exercise during break.
quests.funFact: Many playgrounds have soft ground, like wood chips or rubber, to cushion falls.

quests.instruction: Where can you borrow books to read at school or take home?
quests.hint: Shelves and shelves of books fill this quiet room.
quests.explanation: The library lends books so many students can share them, and you bring them back when you finish.
quests.funFact: Public libraries around the world lend books for free.

quests.instruction: Where do students sit together to eat lunch?
quests.hint: Lunch trays, long tables, and the smell of food are all here.
quests.explanation: The cafeteria is the school's eating place, where students sit and have their meal.
quests.funFact: Some schools call this room the dining hall or the lunchroom.

quests.instruction: You go to school to learn. What are you called?
quests.hint: You share this name with all your classmates.
quests.explanation: A student is someone who goes to school to learn, and every child in the class is one.
quests.funFact: The word 'student' comes from a Latin word meaning 'to study'.

quests.instruction: Who is in charge of the whole school and everyone who works there?
quests.hint: This person leads the whole school, not just one classroom.
quests.explanation: The principal makes sure the school runs well and is safe for students and staff.
quests.funFact: In some countries the principal is called the head teacher.

quests.instruction: Who drives students to school and back home again?
quests.hint: Think about who sits at the front of the bus.
quests.explanation: The bus driver gets students to and from school safely, so everyone should stay seated on the bus.
quests.funFact: Bus drivers check their mirrors and brakes before each trip.

quests.instruction: What does the teacher write on at the front so everyone can see?
quests.hint: It's big, and it hangs on the wall at the front of the room.
quests.explanation: The board is large so the whole class can see what the teacher writes or draws.
quests.funFact: Chalkboards were once common, but many classrooms now use whiteboards.

quests.instruction: What on the classroom wall shows you what time it is?
quests.hint: Its hands move around the numbers 1 to 12.
quests.explanation: A clock helps the class know when it's time to start, finish, or go to lunch.
quests.funFact: The short hand takes 12 hours to go all the way around the clock face.

quests.instruction: Which furniture gives you a flat space to put your notebook while you work?
quests.hint: You rest your work on top of it, and your things may fit inside.
quests.explanation: A desk gives you a steady, flat place for writing and keeping your materials nearby.
quests.funFact: School desks come in different heights so they fit children of different sizes.

quests.instruction: Where do you go at school when you need to use the toilet?
quests.hint: Look for the room with a sign showing a person.
quests.explanation: The washroom is for using the toilet and for washing your hands afterwards.
quests.funFact: Washing your hands for about 20 seconds helps remove germs.

quests.instruction: Which spot in the hallway gives you a cool drink when you press a button?
quests.hint: Water comes up in a little stream when you press.
quests.explanation: A drinking fountain gives you fresh water between lessons, so you don't get thirsty.
quests.funFact: In some places, drinking fountains are called 'bubblers'.

quests.instruction: What do you rub with water on your hands to wash germs away?
quests.hint: It turns into bubbles when you rub it with water.
quests.explanation: Soap lifts dirt and germs off your skin so the water can rinse them away.
quests.funFact: Soap works because it helps dirt and germs slip off your skin.

quests.instruction: Which vehicle takes many students to school each day?
quests.hint: It has many seats because a lot of children ride together.
quests.explanation: A school bus carries many students at once, so it is safe, and it saves time for families.
quests.funFact: School buses have big mirrors so drivers can see all around the bus.

quests.instruction: What rings to tell everyone a lesson is starting or ending?
quests.hint: Its sound is loud enough to hear all around the school.
quests.explanation: The school bell lets everyone know when to start, stop, or change places.
quests.funFact: Schools have used bells to mark lesson times for a very long time.

quests.instruction: Which long indoor path do you walk along to reach your classroom?
quests.hint: Many doors line both sides of it.
quests.explanation: Hallways connect the rooms of the school, so students walk through them calmly and carefully.
quests.funFact: The word 'corridor' comes from an Italian word meaning 'to run'.

quests.instruction: What do you dip into paint to spread color on paper?
quests.hint: Its soft bristles hold the paint and spread it.
quests.explanation: A paintbrush picks up paint and spreads it. Thin brushes are for small details.
quests.funFact: Paintbrushes come in many sizes: thin ones for details, wide ones for big areas.

quests.instruction: Which soft material can you shape into bowls and animals?
quests.hint: You can squeeze and mold it with your hands.
quests.explanation: Clay can be pushed and shaped. When it is baked in a hot oven, it becomes hard.
quests.funFact: Clay comes from the ground, and baking it in a kiln makes it hard.

quests.instruction: Where does your class go for painting and craft projects?
quests.hint: Pictures made by students might hang on its walls.
quests.explanation: In the art room you can try painting, drawing, and making things with different materials.
quests.funFact: Red, yellow, and blue are often called primary colors because artists use them to mix other colors.
